majors.issue: Flagstone yard ground repeats one 16px cell: the same crazy-paving stone shapes recur every cell in rows and columns, so a visible grid shows at 1x. Autocorrelation at 16/32/48 px is about 0.44-0.66 in x and y; the dirt yard gives about 0.25.
majors.evidence: /tmp/vqa-r4-A/t8-flag.png (whole strip, rows of identical stone clusters); /tmp/vqa-r4-A/t5.png, /tmp/vqa-r4-A/t8.png
majors.fix: Draw at least 4-6 interior variants with different stone layouts, chosen by a hash per cell, or draw the paving on a 2x2/3x3 macro tile so that stone joints cross cell borders.

majors.issue: The 'ancient temple ruins' quarter reads as a pristine new plaza. The flagstone is a perfect notched rectangle with an intact curb on every side, with no missing or broken stones, no grass or moss creeping in, and no rubble spill at the edge. The tiny temple stamp sits on it like a dollhouse, so the result is toy-like and not ruined.
majors.evidence: /tmp/vqa-r4-A/t5.png and t8.png: outer border all round; interior uniformly intact
majors.fix: Break up the outer border: let the flagstone fade into grass with patchy and broken stones, gaps, moss and grass tufts in the paving, and rubble at the edge. Make the paving uneven so it is not a clean rectangle.

majors.issue: Nonsense placement: the mine adit (portal with a timber frame) stands on its own on flat packed dirt with no hill or rock face behind it, so it reads like an oven or doghouse. The headframe is placed far from any shaft. Both seeds use the same recipe: a top row of stone house + adit + headframe in a line and a bottom row of scattered props, with half or more of the yard empty dirt.
majors.evidence: /tmp/vqa-r4-A/m7.png (adit centre-left, headframe top-left); /tmp/vqa-r4-A/m2.png (same three in a row, mirrored)
majors.fix: Place the adit against a terrace cliff or rock outcrop, or add a spoil heap or rock backing behind it. Put the headframe over a shaft-mouth piece. Vary the layout between seeds (L/cluster arrangements, ore cart track linking adit and spoil) and shrink the yard to fit what is on it.

majors.issue: Repeated identical stamps: the same vine-block stamp, with the same dead-vine gaps, yellow patch and notched right edge, is pasted 3 times per map. The vines are planted on a bare packed-dirt yard, and the yard (26x15) is mostly empty dirt, so the result reads as a construction lot rather than a vineyard.
majors.fix: Build vine rows procedurally with varied lengths and gaps, or flip or vary the stamps. Put the rows on tilled or grass ground with packed dirt only around the press house and barrels. Shrink the yard to the working area.

majors.issue: Wasteland types do not read as distinct: settlement-4 uses the same recipe as both shanty maps (one horizontal road band, then the same lean-tos, corrugated shacks, solar tables and generators scattered on open dirt at even spacing). Only settlement-1 has the fenced compound that makes a 'survivor settlement' read.
majors.evidence: compare full maps settlement-4.png and shanty-6.png at 1x; /tmp/vqa-r4-A/se4-a.png
majors.fix: Give the settlement a defining structure every seed: a perimeter wall or barricade, a gate, a central yard, watch posts. Give the shanty town dense, clustered, wall-to-wall shacks with narrow alleys.

majors.issue: The shanty town is sparse and laid out on a grid: shelters sit isolated in rows with 2-4 empty cells between them and no alleys or paths, which is the opposite of a shanty town. There are identical stamps side by side: two identical tent-tarps abutting in shanty-3, and three identical lean-tos on one row in shanty-6 (one more below).
majors.evidence: /tmp/vqa-r4-A/sh3-a.png (top centre twin tents); /tmp/vqa-r4-A/sh6-a.png (row y~220-310 tent + two identical lean-tos, plus another lean-to below)
majors.fix: Pack shelters into contiguous clusters that share walls, with scrap fences and trodden-dirt alleys. Do not place the same piece next to itself; vary with shack-a/b/c, container-home and tent alternation.

majors.issue: Does not read as a (zombie) ruined city. The blocks are mostly empty dirt lots holding one or two small, low ruin stamps. There are no sidewalks or curbs, no tall building shells, no blocking wreck pile-ups or barricades, and nothing zombie-specific. The same 2-storey vine ruin and the same slab + flat ruin stamps repeat within each map and across seeds.
majors.evidence: ruined-city-5.png top-centre and centre blocks (same slab+ruin+vine-tower combo twice); ruined-city-2.png overall
majors.fix: Fill blocks edge-to-edge with building footprints and collapsed shells. Add sidewalk/curb edging to the asphalt, plus car pile-ups, barricades and debris blocking streets. Add horror cues (blood, corpses or bags, boarded windows). Vary the ruin stamps.

majors.issue: Ground clutter is uniform confetti: brick bits, gray rubble chunks and yellow tufts are spread at constant density over every dirt cell, with no clustering near ruins or traffic. At 1x this reads as noisy speckle. The dirt base also has a weak 64px repeat (autocorrelation about 0.2-0.24 at 64/128 px).
majors.evidence: /tmp/vqa-r4-A/sh6-dirt.png (even spread of tufts and rubble across the whole strip)
majors.fix: Cluster debris around ruins and walls, and leave calm open ground elsewhere. Cut the decal count by about half. Add larger-scale variation to the dirt (drifts, tracks, darker patches) so that the 64px repeat breaks.

minors.issue: Navy-blue asphalt on brown dirt reads as water channels at first glance (see wl-compare-3x.png and settlement-1). The blue puddle decals placed on the road add to this. It is family-consistent with modern-city, so not a fail.
minors.fix: Desaturate toward blue-grey or charcoal, and add faded lane paint or potholes so the asphalt reads as road.

minors.issue: Two identical green jeeps stacked nose-to-tail in the centre of the vertical road.
minors.fix: Do not repeat the same vehicle within N cells; vary type and orientation, or angle one as a wreck.

minors.issue: Road jog has hard square stair-step corners, and the concrete pad under the water tower has a blocky stair-step outline.
minors.fix: Use the corner mask cells or a diagonal at the jog; round or break the pad outline.

minors.issue: The packed-dirt yard is a large flat area with sparse uniform specks; it is clean but low-interest, and the yard area is oversized for its 7-9 pieces.
minors.fix: Add wheel ruts, footpaths between pieces, darker trampled patches near doors; size the yard to its content.

minors.issue: The temple stamp's roof is drawn as an oblique prism with a visible receding side slope, which leans toward an iso side face (this piece is outside the new yard work).
minors.fix: Redraw the roof as a straight top plane over the pediment front.

minors.issue: Rust on the top plane is a dense scatter of 1-2 px orange specks, which is a bit noisy next to the cleaner shack pieces.
minors.fix: Merge the rust into fewer, larger streaks that follow the corrugation.
